surface_mechanism_description: The surface reaction mechanism involves the adsorption of HfCl4 and H2O on the silicon oxide surface, leading to the formation of HfO2. The reaction is limited by the availability of reactive OH groups on the surface, and the saturation of HfO2 deposition occurs when the surface is fully covered by OH groups. The growth is also influenced by steric hindrance of the adsorbed precursor molecules and the hydroxyl termination of the SiO2 surface.
